# SO THIS IS NOT MY BUG — IT IS A FILE-WIDE ONE, AND MY 18 JOINED IT. 259 of the 277 predate
# today. The pattern was already there: a grey icon gets the Disabled token because the value
# matches, and nobody sees the consequence because it only appears in dark mode.
# MY 18 DID MAKE IT WORSE FOR THEIR OWN NODES, AND THAT IS WORTH BEING EXACT ABOUT. Before the
# rebind those vectors were a STATIC #868686 in both modes, which on a white panel is about
# 3.6:1 — readable. After it they are #F2F2F2 in dark, 1.12:1 — not. Light mode is identical
# either way, so no screenshot in the mode anyone looks at would show it.
# The fix for all 86 is one decision, not eighteen: these are secondary icons, not disabled ones,
# and Icons/Icon - Secondary (#656565 light, #C1C1C1 dark) is the role-correct token. That is a
# designer call on 86 nodes across seven pages, so it is recorded here rather than applied.
# Scope rule plus a DARK-MODE CONTRAST GUARD, over every remaining deprecated style on component
# pages. Collection 1514 -> 1429; 20 edits cleared 85 nodes. Every id is in
# tokens/_raw/deprecated-rebinds-applied.tsv.
# THE GUARD EARNED ITS PLACE ON THE FIRST RUN. It held 13 nodes whose single scope-matched
# candidate would have been unreadable in dark against their own backdrop:
# That is exactly the mistake the Grey #868686 run made 18 times. The rule that found the token is
# the same rule; what changed is that it now has to survive a measurement before it is written.
# ── FOUR COLOURS HAVE NO SEMANTIC AT THEIR VALUE AT ALL ───────────────────────
# The first three are the DARK-MODE values of live semantic tokens — #2C313C is Background/Primary
# in dark, #1D1F27 is Navigation/Nav bg left in dark, #1A1A1A is Progress bar/Border in dark. So
# someone painted a dark-mode colour statically into a light-mode design. There is no token to
# rebind them to, because the thing they want is "the dark value of X", which a variable expresses
# by MODE and not by name. These need redrawing, not rebinding.
# ── THE BIGGEST HOLD IS STILL THE SURFACES ───────────────────────────────────
# Every one of these is a two-or-more-candidate case where the candidates agree in light and differ
# in dark. None can be settled from a light-mode render, which is the whole reason they are listed
# rather than applied.
# The first run of docs/figma-rebind-deprecated.js with WRITE = false, over the nine largest
# styles nobody had swept: White Ivory, Grey dolphin, Black, Light ivory, Orange, Blue ocean (A),
# Colour blue, Red (A), Blue Charade. ONE traversal, 105 nodes outside documentation, two
# agreeing sweeps, NOTHING WRITTEN. What it would do:
# SIX OF 105 ARE MECHANICAL, and they are one case: six Negative-button frame fills that take
# Background/Negative Button. APPLIED in a second run with WRITE = true: Red (A) 16 -> 10, both
# after-sweeps agreeing, all six ids in tokens/_raw/deprecated-rebinds-applied.tsv. Collection
# 1429 -> 1423. The other ten Red (A) nodes hold on three candidates — Icons/Icon - Negative
# #FF8080, Icons/Icon - Required field #5CC4EA and Border/Negative #FF8080 — which is a real
# divergence in dark and a person's call.
# `Colour blue` has 29 references and NONE outside documentation. It is a style guide colour,
# which the by-page split predicted and this confirms node by node.
# GREY DOLPHIN IS 23 STROKES, and every one of them holds on four candidates: Icons/Icon - Primary
# inverted #3E3E3E, Navigation/Nav bg left #1D1F27, Nav bg top #23252E, Icons/Icon - Always white
# #FFFFFF. A white stroke in dark mode is either a hairline that must stay white or one that must
# invert, and nothing in the file says which. This is the second deprecated white, and it is the
# surfaces problem wearing a different hat.
# LIGHT IVORY IS 23 FRAMES, all held on Background/Secondary #1D1F27 vs Table/Stripe cell #23252E
# — a page background and a table stripe, identical in light. BLUE OCEAN is 28 marks held on
# Icons/Icon - Link #5CC4EA vs Charts/Chart 1 #0075BE: a link blue that lightens in dark against a
# chart blue that does not.
# BLUE CHARADE AND BLACK confirm the no-semantic finding node by node: 14 and 2 nodes at #2C313C
# and #1A1A1A, the dark values of Background/Primary and Progress bar/Border painted statically.
# No rebind can express them; they need redrawing.
# AND THE RUN CORRECTED THE RULE'S OWN MESSAGE. The two Orange nodes were held saying the
# candidates "differ in dark" — and Icons/Icon - Warning and Charts/Chart 2 are BOTH #FC8700 in
# dark. The hold was right and its reason was false. Where every candidate resolves the same in
# both modes no render can separate them, so the hold is about MEANING rather than appearance, and
# chooseToken now says which of the two it is. Four mutants.
